async def act(page):
    # Wait for the page to load completely
    await page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')
    
    # Try to find all post elements using accessibility roles
    # First, attempt to find articles, as posts might be structured as articles
    articles = await page.get_by_role('article').all()
    if articles:
        posts = articles
    else:
        # If no articles, try list items, which might contain posts
        list_items = await page.get_by_role('listitem').all()
        if list_items:
            posts = list_items
        else:
            # If still no posts, return an error message
            return 'No posts found on the homepage.'
    
    # Check if there are enough posts for second-to-last
    if len(posts) < 2:
        return 'Not enough posts on the homepage.'
    
    # Get the second-to-last post
    second_last_post = posts[-2]
    
    # Extract the title: look for a link within the post, then a heading
    title = ''
    link_elements = await second_last_post.get_by_role('link').all()
    if link_elements:
        # Use the first link as the title, assuming it's the post title
        title = await link_elements[0].text_content()
    else:
        heading_elements = await second_last_post.get_by_role('heading').all()
        if heading_elements:
            title = await heading_elements[0].text_content()
        else:
            title = 'Title not found'
    
    # Extract the publish date: look for text containing 'Dec' (common in dates) or a time role
    date = ''
    # Use get_by_text with exact=False to find date text
    date_elements = await second_last_post.get_by_text('Dec', exact=False).all()
    if date_elements:
        date = await date_elements[0].text_content()
    else:
        # Try to find a time element
        time_elements = await second_last_post.get_by_role('time').all()
        if time_elements:
            date = await time_elements[0].text_content()
        else:
            # Fallback: search for any text that might contain a date pattern
            all_text = await second_last_post.text_content()
            # Simple heuristic: look for a pattern like 'Dec 26, 2025'
            import re
            date_match = re.search(r'\w{3} \d{1,2}, \d{4}', all_text)
            if date_match:
                date = date_match.group()
            else:
                date = 'Date not found'
    
    # Return the result as required
    result = f'Title: {title}, Publish Date: {date}'
    return result

    # Extract the title: look for a link within the post, then a heading
    title = ''
    link_elements = await second_last_post.get_by_role('link').all()
    if link_elements:
        # Use the first link as the title, assuming it's the post title
        title = await link_elements[0].text_content()
    else:
        heading_elements = await second_last_post.get_by_role('heading').all()
        if heading_elements:
            title = await heading_elements[0].text_content()
        else:
            title = 'Title not found'

    # Extract the publish date: look for text containing 'Dec' (common in dates) or a time role
    date = ''
    # Use get_by_text with exact=False to find date text
    date_elements = await second_last_post.get_by_text('Dec', exact=False).all()
    if date_elements:
        date = await date_elements[0].text_content()
    else:
        # Try to find a time element
        time_elements = await second_last_post.get_by_role('time').all()
        if time_elements:
            date = await time_elements[0].text_content()
        else:
            # Fallback: search for any text that might contain a date pattern
            all_text = await second_last_post.text_content()
            # Simple heuristic: look for a pattern like 'Dec 26, 2025'
            import re
            date_match = re.search(r'\w{3} \d{1,2}, \d{4}', all_text)
            if date_match:
                date = date_match.group()
            else:
                date = 'Date not found'

    # Return the result as required
    result = f'Title: {title}, Publish Date: {date}'
    return result
